minutes.headline: Commission approved DPW's Northville Crossing culvert replacement after a years-long right-of-entry delay was resolved.
minutes.summary: This was a long hearing-heavy Conservation Commission meeting covering two certificates of compliance, several continued wetlands permit hearings for a multi-lot subdivision on Parmenter/Round Road, a proposed multi-year herbicide/vegetation management plan for Marshall Pond, and approval of a long-delayed DPW culvert replacement at Northville Crossing. The commission also worked through several enforcement/violation matters (48 Meadow Lane, a drainage-area violation, 715 Reservoir Road, 314 Highland Street), agreeing on remediation plantings and signage rather than formal violation filings in most cases, and discussed longer-term administrative matters including the conservation budget, a possible riverfront-regulations training session, and future plans for the Hollis Road property.

what_happened.line: The commission approved DPW's Northville Crossing culvert replacement after a years-long right-of-entry delay was resolved.
Four continued hearings on a Parmenter/Round Road subdivision drew resident questions about wetland impact, runoff, and rain-garden maintenance before being pushed to April 15.
A years-long unpermitted clearing violation near Mass Ave was resolved with an accepted planting and phasing plan rather than a formal violation filing.
A proposed multi-year herbicide treatment plan for Marshall Pond was continued to April 15 pending a state DEP file number.
A proposed stormwater utility bylaw was held back from this town meeting cycle given the town's broader budget pressures.

why_it_matters: The culvert approval clears a long-stalled DPW infrastructure project that affects drainage at Northville Crossing.
The Parmenter/Round Road subdivision hearings, and residents' runoff and well-water questions, will keep returning to this board through at least mid-April as more lots move toward permits.
Holding the stormwater utility bylaw back this cycle means any new fee or funding mechanism for stormwater management is delayed to a future town meeting, not decided now.
